title: Descent and test-morphism comparison for fpqc-compatible labelled clopen partitions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\{f_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], with $I$ an arbitrary set. Let $A$ be a set, possibly empty. For every $i$ let $\rho_i:|U_i|\to A$ be a function whose fibres $\rho_i^{-1}(a)$ are open for every $a\in A$. Write $p_i,p_j$ for the projections from $U_i\times_XU_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $\rho_i\circ|p_i|=\rho_j\circ|p_j|$ for every $i,j$. There is a unique family $(Z_a)_{a\in A}$ of pairwise disjoint open and closed subsets of $|X|$ with $\bigcup_{a\in A}Z_a=|X|$ and $f_i^{-1}(Z_a)=\rho_i^{-1}(a)$ for every $i,a$. Give each $Z_a$ its open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. Moreover, for any scheme morphism $h:V\to X$ and any function $\sigma:|V|\to A$, if $\rho_i\circ|q_i|=\sigma\circ|q_V|$ on every $U_i\times_XV$ (where $q_i$ and $q_V$ are the two projections), then $h^{-1}(Z_a)=\sigma^{-1}(a)$ for every $a$. In particular the fibres of $\sigma$ are open and closed. Neither $I$ nor $A$ is assumed finite, and $X$ need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 03N0, label lemma-open-fpqc-covering, applied to every label fibre and its complement; test-morphism comparison uses fpqc base change, Tag 022D, topologies.tex label lemma-fpqc (3); blueprint rank proof, fpqc descent paragraph and independence of trivializing cover

proof.text: For $a\in A$ put $W_{i,a}=\rho_i^{-1}(a)$, an open subset of $U_i$, and give it the open subscheme structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. The assumed equality of label functions on $U_i\times_XU_j$ implies $p_i^{-1}(W_{i,a})=p_j^{-1}(W_{j,a})$: a point belongs to either side exactly when the common label is $a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-subscheme-fpqc-descent] to these compatible opens for each $a$. It gives an open subset $Z_a\subseteq|X|$, with its open subscheme structure, satisfying $f_i^{-1}(Z_a)=W_{i,a}$.

The fpqc definition [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] gives joint surjectivity. For any $x\in|X|$, choose $u\in|U_i|$ over $x$. Then $x\in Z_a$ if and only if $\rho_i(u)=a$. Thus every $x$ belongs to exactly one $Z_a$, proving disjointness and union $|X|$. Hence $|X|\setminus Z_a=\bigcup_{b\ne a}Z_b$ is open and $Z_a$ is also closed. For any competing family, membership at $x$ is determined by its prescribed inverse image at the same $u$, so each competing piece equals $Z_a$. If $A=\varnothing$, a point $x$ would produce the impossible value $\rho_i(u)\in A$, so $|X|=\varnothing$ and the empty family has all the required properties.

For the test morphism $h:V\to X$, apply [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. The projections $q_V:U_i\times_XV\to V$ form an fpqc covering, after exchanging the fibre-product factors by their universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular they are jointly surjective by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. No finiteness or quasi-compactness hypothesis on $V$, $X$, $I$ or $A$ is used.

Given $v\in|V|$, choose $i$ and $w\in|U_i\times_XV|$ with $q_V(w)=v$, using joint surjectivity [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The fibre-product equation gives $h(v)=f_i(q_i(w))$. Therefore $h(v)\in Z_a$ if and only if $q_i(w)\in W_{i,a}$, if and only if $\rho_i(q_i(w))=a$, if and only if $\sigma(v)=a$, the last equivalence using the test compatibility. This proves $h^{-1}(Z_a)=\sigma^{-1}(a)$. A scheme morphism is continuous, so inverse images of the open and closed $Z_a$ are open and closed. This also covers $V=\varnothing$.
